newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-THREE SENT OFF AS OLD RIVALRY BOILS OVER AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-THREE SENT OFF AS OLD RIVALRY BOILS OVER AGAIN.

text.p: Three players were sent off as bitter rivals Gremio and Palmeiras clashed again on Thursday, this time in a Brazilian championship quarter-final, first leg match.
Gremio, playing in their own Olimpico stadium in Porto Alegre, won 3-1 in a match marred by 57 fouls.
In Thursday's other game, Atletico Mineiro came from behind to beat Atletico Paranaense 3-1 at home.
Palmeiras midfielder Leandro was dismissed early in the second half for a second bookable offence, almost immediately after his team had a penalty appeal turned down.
Fifteen minutes later Gremio striker Paulo Nunes, scorer of 14 goals in the tournament, and Palmeiras defender Cleber clashed in the Palmeiras penalty and were both shown the red card.
Palmeiras, regarded as the best team in Brazil, took a first half lead through striker Luizao, who also missed two gilt-edged chances early in the second half.
Emerson then headed Gremio level, Leandro was sent off and Palmeiras collapsed, conceeding two more headed goals by Ze Afonso and Luis Carlos Goiano.
Bad feeling between the two clubs goes to last year, when they clashed in both the Copa Brasil and the South American Libertadores Cup.
Gremio won both meetings, which were marred by violence.
Four players -- three of them from Gremio -- were sent off in the second leg of the Copa Brasil clash.
The first leg of the Libertadores Cup tie in the Olimpico stadium was halted for 20 minutes by a brawl involving the nearly all the players on the field.

Riot police intervened and Carlos Alberto Silva, coach of Palmeiras at the time, accused Gremio's players of inciting police to hit his players. Three players were sent off, Gremio won 5-0 and went on to win the competition.
The two sides clashed again this year in the Copa Brasil, with Palmeiras coming out on top.
